chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, and Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, and al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Hishām ibn Sālim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the tasbih in rukuʿ and sujud. He said: In rukuʿ you say, “Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent,” and in sujud, “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.” The obligatory minimum of that is one tasbih, the sunnah is three, and the merit is in seven.

key_terms.التَّسْبِيحِ: glorification of Allah recited in prayer
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: the more virtuous and meritorious amount
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى: the prescribed tasbih recited in sujud
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: the prescribed tasbih recited in rukuʿ

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum tasbih required in rukuʿ and sujud, and what is the sunnah amount?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed tasbih to be recited in rukuʿ and sujud during salat. It explains the minimum obligatory amount, the sunnah measure, and the more meritorious number, making it an important narration in prayer rulings.
